syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of addition or removal of oxygen, hydrogen or electronegative elements.
Identify the oxidising and reducing agent in a reaction using the classical definitions.

topics.title: Redox reactions in terms of electron transfer

concepts.learning_objective: Explain oxidation as loss and reduction as gain of electrons using half reactions.
Use competitive electron transfer experiments to compare the tendency of metals to release electrons.
Apply the rules to calculate the oxidation number of an element in a compound or ion.
Identify oxidation, reduction, oxidant and reductant from changes in oxidation number.
Classify redox reactions as combination, decomposition or displacement reactions.
Recognise disproportionation reactions and the oxidation states that allow them.

topics.title: Balancing redox reactions, titrations and limitations

concepts.learning_objective: Balance redox equations by the oxidation number and half-reaction methods.
Explain how end points are detected in permanganate, dichromate and iodometric titrations.
Describe a Daniell cell, its electrodes, salt bridge and direction of electron flow.
Use standard electrode potentials to compare oxidising and reducing strengths.

chapters.title: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

topics.title: Tetravalence of carbon, shapes and structural representations

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the hybridisation of carbon to bond angle, bond length and shape of organic molecules.
Interpret complete, condensed and bond-line structural formulas.
Classify organic compounds as acyclic, alicyclic, benzenoid or non-benzenoid aromatic and heterocyclic.
Identify functional groups and members of a homologous series.
Name alkanes and substituted chains by the IUPAC rules of longest chain and lowest locants.
Apply suffixes, prefixes and priority rules to name compounds with functional groups and multiple bonds.
Distinguish chain, position, functional group isomerism and metamerism.
Explain how stereoisomers differ from structural isomers.
Describe homolytic and heterolytic cleavage and the stability and structure of the intermediates formed.
Identify nucleophiles and electrophiles and use curved-arrow notation.

topics.title: Electron displacement effects and types of reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the +I and -I effects of groups.
Use resonance structures and the +R/-R effect to explain properties.
Explain the electromeric effect and hyperconjugation.

topics.title: Methods of purification of organic compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Choose sublimation, crystallisation or a suitable distillation method for a given compound.
Explain differential extraction and chromatography, including the retardation factor.
Detect carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur, halogens and phosphorus in organic compounds.
Calculate the percentage of an element from analytical data.

topics.title: Classification of hydrocarbons and their uses

concepts.learning_objective: Classify hydrocarbons as open-chain saturated, unsaturated, alicyclic or aromatic from structure or formula.
Relate common fuels such as LPG, CNG, LNG and coal gas to their sources.
Identify the structural isomers possible for a given alkane formula.
Predict products of decarboxylation, Wurtz reaction and Kolbe's electrolysis.
Explain physical properties and the substitution, oxidation and aromatisation reactions of alkanes.
Compare the stability of staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane.
Identify alkenes that show geometrical isomerism and compare properties of cis and trans forms.
Predict products of addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes with and without peroxide.
Deduce the structure of an alkene from its ozonolysis products.
Explain the linear structure of ethyne and the acidic character of terminal alkynes.
Describe preparation of ethyne from calcium carbide and the addition of water to alkynes.

topics.title: Aromatic hydrocarbons: structure, aromaticity and preparation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the equal bond lengths and stability of benzene using resonance.
Apply the conditions of aromaticity and Huckel's (4n + 2) rule.
Recall laboratory methods of preparing benzene.

topics.title: Reactions of benzene, directive influence and carcinogenicity

concepts.learning_objective: Identify electrophiles and products in electrophilic substitution of benzene.
Predict the directive and activating or deactivating effect of substituents on a benzene ring.
State the origin and harmful effects of carcinogenic polynuclear hydrocarbons.
